title: Fidelity Cost Sandbox: experiments roadmap and operational playbook
author: Marissa Ortega
content:
Overview:

This page describes the Fidelity Cost Sandbox: a product initiative and operational playbook for running controlled fidelity-versus-cost experiments with customers and internal cohorts. The Sandbox provides a reproducible environment (simulation + live pilot hooks) to quantify latency, token-cost, and quality tradeoffs across fidelity knobs (quantization, KV caching aggressiveness, batching profiles, response truncation, model variants). It combines a lab harness, per-tenant telemetry, billing-stub integration, and an operator UX for experiment orchestration and interpretation.

Goals (primary):
- Provide a low-friction way for product and CS teams to quantify unit-cost vs. fidelity for customer workloads.
- Enable safe, reversible fidelity rollouts with measurable KPIs tied to billing and SLOs.
- Reduce time-to-decision for model variant adoption and quantization rollouts from months to weeks.

Out-of-scope for initial release (MVP):
- Automated contract-level price changes or legal billing flows.
- Cross-region capacity orchestration (will rely on existing routing).

Success metrics (how we'll know this is working):
- Experiment throughput: at least 6 customer pilots run to completion in first 6 months.
- Decision velocity: median time from experiment kickoff to recommended action <= 21 days.
- Cost insight accuracy: simulated token-cost within 8% of pilot-observed cost for 95% of pilot runs.
- Quality regressions detected: shadow-eval captures >= 95% of regressions flagged by manual QA within pilot duration.

Product components and responsibilities:
1) Sandbox API & Orchestrator (product / eng-serving-runtime)
   - Orchestrates traffic split, variant assignment, and telemetry collection.
   - Exposes endpoints to: create experiment, attach tenant(s), define knobs, schedule rollout windows.
2) Lab Harness and Simulator (applied-ml-and-evals)
   - Runs synthetic and replayed traces to estimate cost/latency/quality for a configuration.
   - Provides delta forecasts and counterfactuals.
3) Telemetry Bridge (eng-platform / eng-sre)
   - Tags per-request provenance, fidelity settings, and experiment ids.
   - Ensures cost attribution pipeline receives a synthetic billing stub for pilots.
4) Console UX (eng-developer-experience / product)
   - Experiment dashboard, comparison views, recommended actions, and exportable decision memos.
5) Billing & Compliance Hook (finance-and-legal / security-and-compliance)
   - Hooks to flag pilots for billing isolation and compliance review.

Roadmap (Q2 2030 to Q4 2030):
- Q2 2030 (Discovery & internal pilots)
  - Deliver lab harness v1 with replay capability and basic cost simulator. Owner: Applied ML.
  - API v0: experiment create/list/attach endpoints. Owner: Orchestrator team.
  - Console prototype: experiment timeline and telemetry view. Owner: Developer Experience.
- Q3 2030 (Customer pilots)
  - Pilot runner: traffic split and canary rollback automation. Owner: Serving Runtime.
  - Billing-stub integration for per-pilot cost accounting. Owner: Finance Engineering.
  - Shadow-eval integration for automatic quality alerts. Owner: Applied ML.
- Q4 2030 (Operationalization)
  - Guided recommendations engine (batching + quantization presets) in Console. Owner: Product / Optimize.
  - Pilot-to-rollout playbook and SLA mapping. Owner: Product.
  - Exportable decision memo template and customer-API for experiment results. Owner: Developer Experience.

Experiment catalog (MVP set):
- Quantization sweep: int8/int4 variants across 2 models + quality regression checks.
- Batching policy sensitivity: continuous batching thresholds (25ms/50ms/100ms) and tail-latency impact.
- KV cache aggressiveness: short/medium/long prefix retention and cache hit-rate vs cost.
- Response truncation: token-budget constrained outputs with rerank safety net.
- Variant substitution: fallback to smaller model when tail-latency > threshold.

Operational runbook (step-by-step for a customer pilot):
1. Intake and risk assessment (1–2 days)
   - Fill pilot intake form (customer profile, data sensitivity, expected QPS, SLOs).
   - Security/Legal review for data residency and PII.
2. Lab run (2–5 days)
   - Run replay of representative traces through lab harness; record simulator outputs (cost forecast, latency, quality deltas).
   - Product PM reviews and approves candidate knobs.
3. Sandbox pilot (7–21 days)
   - Provision experiment (API): attach tenant, set traffic split (common default: 10% test / 90% control), define rollback thresholds.
   - Monitor daily dashboards: cost delta, P50/P95 latency, regression alerts from shadow-eval.
   - Automated rollback triggers: quality_regression_rate > 1% OR P95 latency > baseline*1.4 OR daily cost > forecast+20%.
4. Decision & action (1–3 days)
   - Export decision memo describing results, recommended next step (promote, iterate, or cancel).
   - If promote: create rollout plan (canary waves, entitlement mapping, billing adjustments).

SLOs and alert thresholds (pilot default values):
- Quality regression alert: any top-5 prompt-set pass rate drop > 1%.
- Latency SLO deviation: trigger alert when P95 exceeds baseline*1.25 during pilot window.
- Cost forecast deviation: trigger when observed incremental token-cost > forecast + 15% over 24h.

Telemetry & data schemas (summary table):
- experiment_id: string tag applied to all telemetry.
- fidelity_profile: label (e.g., quant-int8, kv-medium, batch-50ms).
- cost_estimate_usd_per_1m_tokens: number (simulator output).
- observed_token_count: integer (per-tenant, per-window).
- shadow_eval_score: float (0–1) and label.
(Full schema in Appendix A: link to /eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/experiment-telemetry-schema)

Console UX: key screens and flows:
- Create experiment form with pre-filled templates (Quantization Sweep, Batching Sensitivity, Cache Policy).
- Live compare: control vs variant metrics over time with exportable CSV.
- Recommendation card: simple pass/fail and recommended action with confidence band.

Billing considerations and guardrails:
- Pilots do not immediately alter customer invoices. Finance will run a billing-stub flow to report hypothetical delta.
- Any pilot that would reduce revenue > 5% must be escalated to commercial lead before rollout.
- Pilot data used for price-change recommendations must include at least 14 days of stable telemetry or a minimum of 100k tokens, whichever is larger.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Simulator mismatch to real traffic -> Mitigation: require short live pilot stage and conservative forecasts (+20% buffer).
- Risk: Hidden quality regressions in long-tail prompts -> Mitigation: include customer-specified prompt-sets and automated random-sampling.
- Risk: Unexpected billing disputes -> Mitigation: finance-stub transparency, exportable reports, and pre-signed customer consent for experiments.

Open questions (to resolve before public beta):
- What guardrails are required for regulated verticals (healthcare/finance)? Proposal: default to restricted confidentiality and require security review.
- How will per-tenant warm-capacity interactions affect cost attribution? Engineering investigation required.

Appendix A — example experiment config (YAML):

---
experiment_id: "fcs-2029-001"
name: "quantization-int4-sweep"
description: "Int4 sweep against model-x using representative traces"
traffic_split:
  control: 90
  variant: 10
knobs:
  - name: "quantization"
    values: ["int8", "int4"]
  - name: "batch_threshold_ms"
    values: [25, 50, 100]
rollout_windows:
  start_date: "2030-03-01"
  end_date: "2030-03-21"
rollback_triggers:
  quality_regression_rate: 0.01
  p95_latency_multiplier: 1.4
  cost_forecast_overrun_pct: 20
telemetry_hooks:
  enable_shadow_eval: true
  experiment_tags: ["quant-sweep", "pilot"]
---
